name: kalshi-history-markets
notes: Structural gates over one `markets` pull of source kalshi-history-crypto (settled history from both archives, 17 fields). It restates suite-kalshi-crypto-markets.json's vocabulary on purpose (a suite must not read its expectations from the source it validates) and adds rules for the three fields the history pack carries beyond the kalshi pack: expiration_value, settlement_ts and volume. What the rule vocabulary cannot say: not_null sees only a null, and the pack writes an ABSENT settlement_ts as '' (empty text), so no rule here catches it; crypto_trading.kalshi_rows:MarketRows excludes such a market by name (no_settlement_ts), because a label without its settlement instant cannot be gated. Run: python -m dskit.onboarding validate --suite configs/suite-kalshi-history-markets.json --snapshot <snapshot-vid> --root <store root>.

rules.notes: An empty pull is a broken pull (wrong series, API change, a cutoff that moved the archive), never a quiet day.

One row per market per pull. The live copy of a market the archive also listed is dropped by the pack WHATEVER its settlement time (the real archive lists markets settled about a day after market_settled_ts, probed 2026-10-07); a duplicate here means that routing failed.
Each of the six series returned at least one settled market. Six restates the series list; the pin test keeps them equal.
The six series the source pulls, RESTATED here on purpose. tests/test_configs.py pins the two lists together.

The source asks for settled markets, so every row should be final: the live API spells it 'finalized' and the archive may spell it 'settled'. Another status is a market whose result and value are not yet known: read it before modelling.

A settled market reads yes or no. '' means unsettled and anything else (void, scalar) is a settlement the calibration must handle by name: fail here so it is decided, then amend the suite (a new, auditable hash).
A value that is neither a known geometry nor empty is a new market type: block until a payoff rule exists. Empty is allowed here and WARNED by markets-strike-type-set.
An EMPTY strike_type is a market never given a strike (settled 15-minute rows of 2026-08 read 'Target price: TBD'): drop it by name, never guess a strike.

Strikes are USD prices of BTC or ETH, far above 100; a negative, non-numeric or sub-100 one is a unit slip. The history archive holds five finalized markets whose floor_strike is the settlement value divided by 10,000: KXBTC15M-26APR131115-15 (7.243729, true 72437.29) and -26APR131130-30 (7.198773), KXETH15M-26APR131115-15 (0.22348), -30 (0.222165) and -45 (0.221499), probed 2026-10-07: they are EXPECTED here (runbook section 5) and the spot node refuses them as anchors and as priced strikes (basis_range, max_abs_log_moneyness). A new name in this list is a new slip: read it before modelling.
As floor_strike, for the upper edge of a range or a 'less' market (the same unit-slip floor of 100 USD).

The realised settlement value: the CF Benchmarks 60-second average, the continuous label. Null means the venue sent none (or a non-number) for a market that should be final. Warn: the yes/no result still labels the row, and MarketRows carries the value only when it is there.
A BTC or ETH index level in dollars cannot be negative; a negative or non-numeric value is a unit slip or a parse fault. Null is skipped (see the rule above).
The market's whole-life contracts (volume_fp). Null means the venue omitted it. It is known only after the end of the market: never a feature at a decision.
A contract count cannot be negative.
A market dated at its close cannot be dated after it was acquired; the pack dates an unfinished one at the capture minute.
